Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 103, verses 1–3:

Makkiyyah (Meccan), and it has sixty-eight letters, fourteen words, and three verses.

Abu Kamil ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mutar informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sharik narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Muslim, from his mother, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the Surah of Wal-'Asr, Allah will end his life with patience, and he will be with the companions of truth on the Day of Resurrection" [254] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/434.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By time,﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "By the age (al-dahr)." Ibn Kaysan said: "The night and the day," and it is said that both are called "the two 'asrs" (al-'asran), and the morning and the evening are also called "the two 'asrs." Humayd ibn Thawr said:

"The two 'asrs will not linger for a day and a night, when they seek to overtake what they have aimed at."

Al-Hasan said: "From the decline of the sun until its setting." Qatadah said: "The last hour of the hours of the day." Muqatil said: "The prayer of 'Asr, which is the middle prayer."

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss,﴾ except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for indeed they are not in loss.

﴿And advise one another﴾ — they urge one another and enjoin one another. ﴿to truth﴾ — to the Qur'an, according to al-Hasan and Qatadah.

Muqatil said: "To faith and monotheism." It was said: "To act upon the truth."

﴿And advise one another to patience﴾ — in performing the obligations and upholding the command of Allah. Ibn 'Awn narrated from Ibrahim, who said:

He meant that a human being, when he lives long in this world and grows old, is in decline, weakness, and regression, except for the believers, for their rewards and the good deeds they used to do in their youth, strength, and health will be recorded for them. This is like His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature; then We reduced him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe﴾ [[Surah al-Tin: 4–6.]] etc.

He said: [Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) used to recite it]: "Indeed, mankind is in loss," and he is in it until the end of time. And likewise it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud.

Ali used to recite it: "By time, and the calamities of time, indeed mankind is in loss, and he is in it until the end of time" [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/371, at the verse.]].

The correct recitation is that upon which the common people and the codices agree.

Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Khatib informed us, by reading to him, in Rajab of the year 386 (AH), saying: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Dalan narrated to us, saying: Al-Qadi Mansur ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Dawud ibn Sulayman al-Dinawari narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn 'Alqamah narrated to us, saying:

Sabat ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Rufay'ah, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: I recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) "Wal-'Asr," and I said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah, what is its interpretation?"

He said: "By time, an oath from Allah, He swears to you by the end of the day." ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ — he said: "Abu Jahl ibn Hisham." ﴿except those who believe﴾ — "Abu Bakr al-Siddiq." ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ — "Umar ibn al-Khattab." ﴿and advise one another to truth﴾ — "Uthman ibn Affan." ﴿and advise one another to patience﴾ — "Ali ibn Abi Talib" [255] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/180.]].

And Abd al-Khaliq [ibn Ali] informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Yusuf ibn Hatim ibn Nadr informed us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Uthman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hisham Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, saying: My paternal uncle Ali ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, from his father Rifa'ah, who said: I performed Hajj and came upon Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn Abbas delivering a sermon on the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he recited: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿By time. Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ — "Abu Jahl ibn Hisham." ﴿except those who believe﴾ — "Abu Bakr al-Siddiq." ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ — "Umar ibn al-Khattab." ﴿and advise one another to truth﴾ — "Uthman ibn Affan." ﴿and advise one another to patience﴾ — "Ali ibn Abi Talib" [256] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/180.]].
